transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um... well, I guess what brings me in is... it's a little embarrassing, honestly. It's probably not a huge deal, but I just wanted to get your opinion on it, if that's okay? 

I've been having this issue where I keep getting up when I'm supposed to just... stay put. Like, I'll be in the middle of a client interview—I'm a private investigator—or, you know, during tutoring sessions, or even just sitting at my book club. I just sort of pop out of my chair. People are really starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen like everyone else. I try to play it off like I just need to stretch or grab a glass of water, but... I don't know, does that make sense as a reason to come in? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting.

When you feel the urge to get up and move, is it usually because you're feeling worried or nervous about something, or does it feel more like a general restlessness or need to move that isn't tied to any particular worry?

Oh, um... I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't think I'm worried? I mean, I really hope I'm not just sitting there being anxious without realizing it. I think it's just... I don't know, maybe just a little extra energy? 

It's not a bad feeling, really, just sort of this... this urge that I should probably stand up for a second. I'm definitely not sitting there stressing over my cases or anything like that when it happens. It's just a mild restlessness, I guess. Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, get easily distracted, or forget details even when you're trying to pay attention?

Oh, um... no, I don't think I have that problem. I actually pride myself on being a really good listener. I mean, with my work, I really have to catch all the little details, you know? So I'm usually very dialed in to what people are saying. 

I don't really lose focus or forget things... at least, not any more than anyone else might on a really busy day, I think? I hope that's okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. But no, paying attention is usually fine for me, it's really just the... the staying in the chair part that I struggle with. Did I explain that right?
Thinking back, do you remember having this same kind of restlessness or difficulty staying seated back when you were a child, like in school?

Oh... um, yeah, actually. I guess I was always a little bit like that. I mean, my grade-school report cards always made a point to say I was a really bright kid—which is a good thing, right? But... well, they usually also mentioned that I had a hard time staying in my seat or waiting my turn. I really wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything, I promise! I think I was just... eager? 

My mother actually still jokes about it. She says I treated every single classroom like a crime scene that I just had to pace through. It's mostly just a funny family joke now, but... does that help answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of background.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others feel is necessary, interrupting people, or blurting out responses before they've finished speaking?

Oh, um... I guess I do talk a bit? But I really try not to be rude about it! I know you mentioned interrupting, and I really hope I don't do that too much. I always want to be polite. 

It's just... well, in my line of work, you really have to talk through every possible angle of a case, you know? And sometimes I'll be in a client meeting, and I just... I kind of keep going? Like, I'll catch myself talking through every single detail until I've basically filled all the space in the conversation. And sometimes I can tell they're giving me clear signs that they're done, or that they get the point, but I just have this... this momentum, I guess? 

I really don't mean to talk over anyone or be too much. I just want to make sure I'm being thorough for them. Is that... does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible conversationalist!

Would you say these patterns of restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty staying still have caused ongoing problems in more than one area of your life—like at work, in relationships, or socially—for at least the past six months?

Oh... um... I really wish I could say it hasn't. I take my job so seriously, and I always want to do good work. But... well, if I'm being completely honest—and I know I need to be totally honest with you to get this right—it has been causing some issues. Definitely for the last six months, maybe even longer. 

I know I said earlier that I'm great with details, and I usually try so hard to be! But... recently, because I get so wound up and just kind of barrel through things, I've actually... well, I've missed a few details in my investigations. It is so incredibly embarrassing to admit that out loud. I really think it's starting to cost me professionally. 

And... well, I've definitely irritated some clients when I get too intense or talk too much. Plus, the junior detectives I work with... I've noticed they're a lot less willing to debrief with me after a case lately. I think they feel a bit steamrolled when I get pacing around the room and talking over them, even though I really, really don't mean to make them feel that way! I always want to be a supportive mentor to them. 

Does that... make sense? I hope I don't sound like a completely awful investigator. I'm really trying my best, I promise. Am I answering your question okay?
Have you ever had a distinct period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually elated, high-energy, or needed much less sleep than normal, separate from your usual day-to-day restlessness?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely have days where I'm really focused on a case and maybe stay up a little later than I should, but... not like what you're describing. I don't think I've ever felt, like, unusually high-energy or anything like that for days on end. 

I usually try to get my full eight hours of sleep, even if I'm feeling restless. I know how important rest is for doing a good job! So, no, I haven't really had any periods like that. Is that a good thing? I hope that's the right answer... I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of what's going on.
Do you regularly consume a lot of caffeine, energy drinks, or take any stimulant medications or supplements that might contribute to this restlessness?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I really try to be careful about what I put in my body. I mean, I'll have just a regular cup of coffee in the morning to start my day, but I never touch those energy drinks. I know they can be so bad for you! And I definitely don't take any sort of supplements or... or medications like that either. 

I always try to stay as healthy as possible so I can do a good job for my clients. So, it's really just... well, just me being naturally this wound up, I suppose. 

Is that... I mean, is it helpful that I don't drink much caffeine? I really hope I'm doing the right thing by avoiding all that stuff!

Aside from the times you feel the urge to get up and move, do you often find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things—like your work, health, or other everyday matters—more days than not?

Oh... um, worrying excessively? Well, I mean... I do care a lot about my work, and I always want to make sure I'm doing a thorough job. So I guess I think about my cases quite a bit, but... I wouldn't call it excessive worrying, exactly. 

I just... I like to be prepared, you know? I want to be the best investigator I can be for my clients. So maybe I double-check things in my head, but it's not like I'm sitting around panicked about my health or everyday chores or anything like that. It's really just the restlessness that gets in my way, not so much... anxiety or worry. 

I try to stay positive and focused on the facts! Does that sound okay? I really don't want you to think I'm just a bundle of nerves all the time. I'm actually a very capable person, I promise!
